title: Tobacco retailer density around secondary schools and student smoking and vaping: a cross-sectional analysis
subtitle: Students within schools, 2025 school health survey linked to the state licence list
statement: Several councils want to cap tobacco retail licences near schools, and the minister's office has asked whether students at schools with more licensed retailers nearby are more likely to smoke or vape. The state has a geocoded licence list and a 2025 school health survey; linking them allows a cross-sectional estimate of the association, adjusted for school socioeconomic status and remoteness, that is honest about what it cannot show.
whoAffected: Secondary students, their families, licensed retailers near schools, councils considering caps, and the minister's office deciding whether to back them.
whatHurts: Youth smoking and vaping start habits that last; a cap that does not reduce use would cost retailers and councils without benefit, while no action would leave dense retail environments around some schools.
currentPractice: Licences are issued without regard to distance from schools; the survey and the licence list have never been linked.
whyNow: Councils are drafting caps and the 2025 survey is the first wave collected after licensing started.
constraints: Secondary data only: the licence list and the 2025 school health survey. One analyst for four months from January 2027. School and student identities stay with the survey custodian; analysis only through the custodian's secure analysis service.
patientCenteredGoal: Students grow up with fewer opportunities and prompts to start smoking or vaping, and policy rests on honest evidence.
summary: Problem framed as a cross-sectional linkage of retailer density to student smoking and vaping.
